page1.text:
"—, —, —"
It's only a matter of time until the cave collapses.
The ceiling is crumbling all over, and the barren field is turning into a mountain of rubble.

page2.text:
"—, —, —"
My joints are stiff.
It hurts to bend my arms and legs.
My nerves are hot.
Hundreds of blades are sprouting from my body.
It's an execution I can't escape from.
My body is made of swords.
I've always known that.
The fuse was lit on the time bomb ever since I used Projection.
This ending was set a long time ago.

page3.text:
"...Hah, ah...!"
I'm going to break.
Any more, and I'll break.
I'll crumble to pieces, just like the falling rocks.

page4.text:
...But I can still make it.
This body is sluggish, but if I can stop it all here, this day won't have been for nothing.

page5.text:
A one-day lease on life.
It doesn't sound like much, but right now, it's something I long for.
Just one day. One hour. Even one minute.
If I'm going to live, I want to live as long as I can, appearances be damned.

page6.text:
"Hah, zzrgh...!"
Cracks appear.
Not outside, but inside my forebrain.
The part that controls my behavior principles and sense of pleasure.
The most important part of really being alive. Life is the pursuit of pleasure. Without it, humans are just beasts.

page7.text:
"Hah, ah."
I wouldn't say it's convenient.
But it'll still be missed.
I bite my fingers to remind myself that I'm still me.
Still, I'm cracking.
I can't stop the agony of loss and the disappearance of my memories.

page8.text:
With each step forward, I disappear.
This isn't going to work.
By the time I get there, I won't even remember who I am or what I'm supposed to do.
So, I should stop here and wait for...

page9.text:
"...Yeah, I remember."
But, something.
A big reason. Outside my body.
"Sakura... Let's go look at the flowers."
You have to. You have to. Do your duty.

page10.text:
Time has stopped.
There's no pain.
A single step takes an entire day.
I forget how to breathe.
There's no pain.
I can spend a whole day without taking a single breath.
I lose all meaning.
There's no...what's pain, again?
Living switches to nonliving.
I stop.
I catch myself on a wall as I fall.
It's very small. A tiny foothold contains my entire existence.
It won't hold.
My foothold. Crumbles.

page11.text:
I lose my behavior principles.
I lose my driving motivations.
I lose my raison d'être.
I don't feel afraid.
I've lost what and whom I exist for.

page12.text:
I'm not alive anymore.
No matter what the reason was, my arms don't move for it.

page13.text:
"Trace... (Begin...)"
Words come out.
My neocortex and the other three portions of my cerebrum—never mind my speech center—disappear, but something still remains.

page14.text:
"...on. (...Projection.)"
My body is dead.
But my soul is still here.

page15.text:
I weave eight counts.
The burden shifts from my body to my soul, and meaning—
"...Oh."
That's how Shirou Emiya died.
The shape that stands up is no different from a machine.
It has the function to swing a sword, but it's a husk without a will to move it.

page16.text:
But even without a man-made mind...
In this world, there are many machines that dream.

page17.text:
There was a promise.
Once winter is over and spring comes...
